description.narrative: The project is implemented in the Philippines. The main outcome areas it contributes to are, Countering the threats to democracy and human rights, Advancing equality and worker's rights, Sustainability through a just transition and Opposing the backlash increasing gender equality. The main right holders are migrants and their families, human rights and labor rights defenders and community-based organisations in 3 municipalities/cities. Through capacity building in terms of knowledge and skills for CBOs on migrants' rights, governance, case management, access to justice, social movement unionism, organisational development processes and sustainable green reintegration, cooperative building and skills on organisational development the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas. Also by stakeholding/Constituency building among migrants and families in the Philippines and abroad, Networking and alliance work/partnership building with local stakeholders to strengthen CBOs, mainstream migrant rights, contribute to movement building and sustainable green reintegration to break the vicious cycle of migration and contribute to local initiatives for sustainable development and climate change.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Center for Migrant advocacy CMA and The Palme Center. CMA's vision is a society where justice, good governance, equal opportunity and gender equality prevail and where migrants enjoy equal rights and protection regardless of nationality, ethnicity, religion, gender, occupation or residency status. It aims to promote the rights of overseas Filipino workers and their families and intends (strategic intent) to be a leader in Filipino migration through policy advocacy, information dissemination, networking, capability-building and direct assistance. Its core values are leadership, empowerment, cooperation, integrity and effectiveness. CMA was founded in December 2002 by a group of migrant, women and human rights' advocates, including former overseas Filipino workers and Filipino immigrants, because of the lack of civil society organisations focused on policy advocacy for migrant rights and welfare. CMA is part of rights-orientated networks in the Philippines and abroad and works with a broad network of both government and civil society organisations including trade unions in the country and abroad.Other Donors to the Organisation2023 CMA was supported by AWO Germany, Friedrich Ebert Stiftung (FES), Fund for Global Human Rights, Verite Southeast Asia, Governance in Justice (GoJust)-UNOPS.Project ObjectiveStrengthen capacities of community-based migrant organisations and rural-based groups in three municipalities/cities of Nueva Ecija (Laur, Lupao and Palayan City) for effective protection of migrant rights in the different stages of migration, sustainable green reintegration and participation in movement-building. From 2021 the focus has shifted more to sustainable green integration.Actor groupsThe main actors within each actor group are government agencies, law makers and Academic/training institutions such as CLSU, ATI, PhilRICE, CDA (decision-makers). The Philippine Migrant Rights Watch (PMRW),the Migrant Forum in Asia, Philippine Alliance of Human Rights Advocates (PAHRA), Philippine Migrant Health Network, Freedom from Debt Coalition, the Right to Know Right Now Coalition and the Clean Clothes Campaign South East Asia(actors working in cooperation) Filipino migrant workers, particularly the overseas Filipino workers, with special focus on the women migrant workers/domestic workers and other low-skilled migrant workers (rights holders).
